title: Quadratic Gaussian tail asymptotics
statement: Let $\Phi(t)$ be the standard Gaussian cumulative distribution function and set $L(t)=2\log(1/\Phi(t))$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm. Then $L(t)/t^2$ tends to $1$ as $t$ tends to $-\infty$.
replaced:
Let $\Phi(t)=\int_{-\infty}^{t}e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}\,dx$ and $L(t)=2\log(1/\Phi(t))$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm. Then
\[
\lim_{t\to-\infty}\frac{L(t)}{t^2}=1.
\]
